rationale: Stations barred from live trading regardless of what any re-score concludes. This is a risk ruling, not a profit optimization, and the distinction is load-bearing: every mechanical screen we tested has no predictive power out of sample (see measured_note), so a list that regenerates itself from recent ROI would be noise with a config file around it. This list is entered by hand, cites its evidence, and only a human edits it.
measured_note: 2026-08-30, 332 settlements over 15 days (2026-08-15..29), first half fits the rule and the second half scores it, on the 29 stations with at least 3 first-half settlements. Excluding first-half ROI<=-8% returned -11.0% against a -4.3% baseline; |centre bias|>0.8 returned -9.8%; claim-ratio outside [0.88,1.18] returned -4.0%. A permutation test drawing the same number of stations at random matched or beat every one of them 54-71% of the time, so none of the three carries signal. The hand-picked list below is the exception that motivated the file: it returned -43.3% in the second half against +20.8% for the rest, and random 9-station draws are that bad 1.4% of the time. That test is contaminated by hindsight if the list was read off a full-sample scoreboard, but it was not: LTAC is +13.0% full-sample and named anyway, while RKSI (-70.9%), KAUS (-74.4%), FACT (-66.9%) and EDDM (-52.7%) are worse and not named. The selection is therefore judgement about the stations, not about the leaderboard, and it is recorded as such.

watchlist_not_excluded.rationale: Persistently negative in both halves but not named by the operator. Recorded so the next review starts from evidence rather than from memory; they are NOT barred, because nothing measured says a mechanical extension of the list would help.

authority: operator ruling 2026-08-30, for the 2026-09-01 live open
